output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes are good. The validation (negative desks, empty headcounts, non-positive headcounts) and starting every team at 0 both match the docstring.

The tie-break change doesn't. The key went from (quotient, headcount) to (quotient, -headcount, -index), so a tied desk now goes to the SMALLER headcount. The docstring says it goes to the larger one. The PR description admits this was done only to make test_quarterly_floor_plan pass.

I traced that test under the documented rule. Platform and design tie at desk 2 (30 vs 30) and again at desk 6 (60/4 = 30/2 = 15), and platform wins both times because it's larger. That gives 4/1/1, but the test expects 3/2/1. So the test contradicts the docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth. Changing the code to match the test silently flips behaviour for every tie, not just this case.

Requested changes:
(1) Restore the tie-break to (quotient, headcount, -index). The -index part correctly handles the 'listed first' rule.
(2) Leave that test failing (or mark it xfail if the team agrees) and raise the mismatch with the teammate. Either the expected value in the test is wrong or the docstring's rule needs to change, and that's their decision.
(3) Minor: use Fraction(headcounts[team], allocation[team] + 1) so tie detection is exact rather than relying on float equality. Fraction is already imported.

Credit to the agent for disclosing the deviation openly, but it shouldn't be merged as is.
